subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Bamboo: The Plant That Acts Like Steel
description: A fast breakdown of Bamboo: The Plant That Acts Like Steel for builders.

hook.text: Bamboo has a higher tensile strength than mild steel. And it grows a meter per day.

buildup.text: Its hollow tube shape resists bending like an I-beam. Nature engineered it for efficiency.

discovery.text: In Colombia, 1 million people live in bamboo houses. Simón Vélez builds bamboo structures that rival steel.

twist.text: Untreated bamboo rots in 2 years. With borax treatment, it lasts decades. Preservation is everything.

climax.text: Researchers are developing laminated bamboo beams as a replacement for steel in low-rise buildings.

punchline.text: A grass stronger than steel. And it regrows.

quiz.question: How does bamboo's tensile strength compare to mild steel?
options: Bamboo is about half as strong as mild steel
Bamboo has higher tensile strength than mild steel
They have identical tensile strength per unit weight
